messages:
Maria G: Heads-up: ran a first-pass bring-up for the new oryx-11b int6 profile (QAT-lite) on a representative longform summarization slice. Quick TL;DR: quality drop vs our 13B fp16 baseline is measurable on longform (ROUGE-L delta ~ -0.08), but cost drops a lot (~64%) and p95 latency improves ~35%.
Sam C: can you paste the slice + raw numbers?
Maria G: sure, short table here: Baseline(13B fp16): cost ≈ $25 per 1M tokens, p95=420ms, ROUGE-L=0.62. Oryx-11b-int6: cost ≈ $9 per 1M tokens, p95=270ms, ROUGE-L=0.57. Sample size 3k prompts, avg request ~180 tokens, tail requests up to 800.
Jon P: interesting. Did you check multi-turn coherence? last time int6 hurt multi-turn brevity and factuality.
Maria G: we ran a 500-session multi-turn subset — observed ~3x increase in short factual errors on step 3+. Mostly on knowledge-heavy queries, less so on formatting tasks.
Priya S: product/GTN question: is the user-visible delta big enough that we'd see engagement differences? we need a rollout plan that product can ship without user backlash.
Eva L: exactly — GTN will want a clear opt-in vs default story. If we can show a targeted economy mode that only affects background non-core tasks, that might fly. Need unit econ numbers to justify.
Maria G: quick econ math: per-1M tokens we save ~$16. If a feature cohort produces 50M tokens/mo, that's ~$800/mo savings for that cohort. If we route 30% of traffic to int6 economy mode, rough platform savings ~ $240/mo for 50M base. Scale accordingly. (numbers rough; I can give breakdown by slot).
Luis R: note: int6 has higher KV-cache miss sensitivity on our runtime; warmstarts matter. On small sequences the p95 improvements are clean, but cold-paths show larger variance. We should watch p99 tail during canary.
Sam C: routing proposal: route by request length + signal on 'needs_high_fidelity' (schema from product). Short, high-confidence prompts => int6. Long or knowledge prompts => fp16.
Priya S: suggested routing config (pseudo):
```yaml
routing_rules:
  - if request_tokens <= 200 and signal.needs_high_fidelity == false:
      model: oryx-11b-int6
  - if request_tokens > 200 or signal.needs_high_fidelity == true:
      model: nova13b-fp16
  - fallback: nova13b-int8
  - canary: 5% traffic with auto-rollover on metrics OK
```
Maria G: exact thresholds I'm proposing: start with 200 tokens cutoff, 5% canary, 10% ramp for 2 weeks, holdback 10% control. Gate rollout on these checks: scorecard.delta_ROUGE > -0.07 (block if worse), hallucination_rate delta < +2pp, p95_latency change < +10ms for high-fidelity routes.
Jon P: small ask: can we run a focused A/B on longform summarizer only (user-visible metric = completion-sharing rate)? That isolates engagement.
Eva L: yes — product will accept an economy mode if we can show NIL impact on completion-sharing and a demonstrable cost ROI for operations. Also request a simple copy: "Economy mode reduces inference latency and cost; some longform fidelity tradeoffs may occur."
Maria G: monitoring checklist to ship with canary: [scorecard.delta_ROUGE, hallucination_rate, fallback_rate, p95_latency, p99_latency, cost_per_token, user_engagement_delta]. Alerts: fallback_rate > 2% or scorecard.delta_ROUGE < -0.08 -> immediate rollback.
Luis R: infra notes: make sure KV pre-warm for the canary cohorts, and enable trace sampling (1%) for hallucination triage. Also add per-route cache hit metric.
Priya S: rollout steps summary: 1) 1% shadow for 48h, 2) 5% canary (7d), 3) 10% ramp (14d), 4) evaluate metrics and GTN acceptance.
release-bot: Deployment scheduled: canary bundle oryx-11b-int6 -> infra/stage at 2026-04-02T03:10:00Z (automated note).
Maria G: thanks all — I'll attach the raw slice CSV + eval scripts to the ticket and run the 1% shadow tonight. Will also produce a single-slide unit-econ brief for GTN with the numbers above.
Jon P: ping me when the shadow is up, I'll run the longform-only AB.
Eva L: I'll draft the GTN blurb once I have the brief. :+1:
Maria G: noted. Next sync after canary results. :rocket:
